newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates up but banks shy away from mkt.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates up but banks shy away from mkt.

text.p: Philippine banks quoted on Tuesday higher bid and offer rates for T-bills in the secondary market in line with the auction results, traders said.
But banks were not keen on positioning due to the volatility in the currency market.
"There's still uncertainty in the market even if the July inflation was low. Banks are still cautious to come in," a trader said.
Banks were wary lest liquidity tightened further after the central bank imposed a two-percentage point liquidity reserve against bank deposits and trust funds to contain peso speculation.
Traders said banks would rather invest in cash management bills and make a quick trading gain. An auction for those bills, with terms of 35 and 42 days, will be held later.
The average interbank call loan rate increased to 20.9375 percent from 20.625 percent due to the effect of the additional liquidity reserves, dealers said.
Volume fell to 20.21 billion pesos from 20.63 billion, with 32 lenders and 23 borrowers.
